_why: The ONE place a model or an effort is chosen. Skill and agent frontmatter, .claude/settings.json, .claude/workflows/build-change.js and the panel's lane_types (.clauductor/panel.json) cannot read this file, so each restates what it needs, and .claude/checks/model-roles.sh fails when any of them disagrees with it. Before a single file held the choice, it lived in five places and drifted: a workflow's commit trailer named a retired model while the playbook described a different session model. Change a role here, then run the check and fix what it names.

session.does: the conversation with the owner; orchestrates lanes

builder.does: implements one task group; applies fixes

reviewer.does: reviews one task group; never edits

reviewer-docs.does: reviews a prose-only PR (merge-pr, review-lane.sh); never edits

mechanic.does: build-change preflight, gate, commit, receipt: run a script and quote it

researcher.does: read-only research: no Bash, Edit or Write

helper.does: any other subagent (Explore, general-purpose), via CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL

tiers._why: A change's proposal.md declares **Risk:** low | normal | high, and the owner approves the tier with the design. build-change runs a role that has a `tiers` entry for the declared tier on that variant instead of the role's own model and effort; normal, and any tier a role does not list, is the role itself. .claude/checks/model-roles.sh holds build-change.js's TIERS table to these variants.

economy._why: Quota economy mode. When the panel's quota is past its threshold it writes the file below as {"economy": true, "since": <unix>, "reason": "..."}; build-change reads it at run time and runs each role listed here one tier down. Only roles that are not critical drop: the reviewer and the planner never do (a cheaper review is a weaker gate, a cheaper design a worse decision), and .claude/checks/model-roles.sh fails if either is listed, or if an entry is not strictly cheaper than its role.

lanes._why: Each lane type of the local panel (.clauductor/panel.json `lanes`) and the role its interactive session starts on, restated there as `lane_types` because the panel cannot read this file. Every lane is a session the owner can talk to; the skills it runs switch to their own role.

attribution._why: The trailer every commit Claude writes ends with, when enabled: build-change's commits, merge-pr's squash body, session-close's PR. Name the model you actually run so the history says which one wrote what; set enabled to false if your project keeps commits unattributed.

provenance._why: AI provenance trailers (item 14 of the change process): every squash commit merge-pr lands carries Change:, Agent-Role:, Model: and Session: trailers, so the history says which change, which role, which model and which session wrote it. pr-merge-guard refuses a merge whose --body lacks them while enabled is true. Set it to false to keep commits unattributed.

prices._why: List prices in US dollars per million tokens, for .claude/change-cost.sh (a change's cost against its budget). The key is a model id PREFIX, the longest match wins. A cache write costs 1.25x input for 5 minutes and 2x for an hour. An estimate at list price, not a bill; update it when prices change (claude-api skill, Current Models).
